title: TSMC Stock (TSM) Falls 2.0% as Chip Stocks Slide (Nov 25)
summary: TSMC stock (TSM) fell 1.96% to $342.34 on Nov 25 as AI chip stocks slid after the rally on Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO faded.
body_markdown:
## Why TSMC Stock Fell


The reports reviewed for this article named no TSMC-specific news behind the drop. According to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/25/nvidia-ai-stock-tech-selloff.html) , tech and AI-linked stocks sold off on Wednesday, led by Nvidia and other chip names, as the rally on Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO faded on renewed concerns about AI spending and profitability. CNBC added that Nvidia had one of its best days on record on Monday, November 23, and[has fallen since](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-nvda-stock-news-november-25-2026/) , while tech stocks recovered from steeper losses earlier in the session.


As reported by[GuruFocus](https://www.tradingview.com/news/gurufocus:097f16b74094b:0-tsmc-stocks-slide-6-65-as-taiwan-lands-on-us-tariff-list/) , TSMC's Taipei-listed shares had already fallen on November 25 as Taiwan's market closed lower on renewed AI doubts. GuruFocus read the US move as investors selling AI exposure rather than reacting to TSMC news. Venu Krishna, head of US equity strategy at Barclays, told CNBC that the market is signaling "the AI growth narrative has hit a wall."


## TSM Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- According to[TSMC's October 2026 revenue report](https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3349) , consolidated revenue was approximately NT$586.89 billion, up 14.7% from September 2026 and 59.7% from October 2025.
- The same report shows January through October 2026[revenue](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-revenue-in-finance/) of NT$4,485.62 billion, up 43.3% from the same period in 2025.
- GuruFocus reported that TSMC guided fourth-quarter revenue to US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion, after third-quarter 2026 revenue rose 50.9% to NT$1.494 trillion with a gross margin of 66.4%.


### Risks


- CNBC reported renewed concerns about AI spending and profitability, the theme behind the day's chip sell-off.
- GuruFocus reported that Washington named Taiwan among 14 economies facing proposed excess-capacity tariffs; rates for partners with deals are expected to stay within existing caps, including 15% for Taiwan, and the proposal still faces comment and a hearing.
- Per CNBC, a hot[inflation reading](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/stock-market-today-nasdaq-falls-ahead-of-pce-data/) raised concern that higher interest rates could weigh on demand for growth stocks, including tech.


GuruFocus noted that TSMC's November revenue, due in early December, is the next check.
